general.title: General
general.languageHint: It changes right away and is remembered.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: brnch looks for each agent on this machine and checks it with its own command.
agents.pendingVerification: Flags and output format still to be verified
agents.ownKey: Each agent's login or API key is its own and it needs it to work. brnch protects git credentials, not the agent's.
agents.defaultAgentHint: Preselected when you create a run.
agents.defaultPermissionHint: What an agent may do without asking you.

security.title: Security
security.description: Agents do not need your git token to publish. Here you see whether they can be confined.
security.activeHint: Agents start confined. If isolation stopped being available, they would not run.
security.inactive: No isolation available: agents will not run
security.unknown: The state could not be read.
security.agentKey: The agent's own login or API key is out of scope: it needs it to work.

items.agent: The keys of your SSH agent

security.neverUnconfined: Do not run agents without isolation
security.neverUnconfinedHint: If no isolation is available, the agent does not start. It cannot be turned off.
security.measuredNote: "Check now" leaves a test file in your home folder, asks a confined process to read it and removes it. It measures this machine, right now.
security.measuredWritable: The confined agent could still write in its workspace.
security.measuredNotWritable: The confined agent could NOT write in its workspace.

windows.setupHint: Creates the local account agents run under. Windows asks for administrator permission once.
windows.keyHint: The agent runs as another account, so it does not see your Claude login. Give it an API key; it is kept protected for you and passed only to the agent.
windows.keySaved: Saved. New agents will receive it.

credentials.prefix: For which repositories (it must start with the host)
credentials.tokenHint: On GitHub: Settings › Developer settings › Fine-grained tokens, with read and write on Contents and Pull requests. brnch hands it to gitd once and never sees it again.
credentials.sshNote: Already using SSH with GitHub? gitd does not use your .ssh folder: it reads the repository over HTTPS with this token, even when it is written as git@github.com:…, and agents never receive it.
